root_cause.text: The AppArmor DFA blob may not be 8-byte aligned when sourced from userspace or kernel, causing the code in `aa_dfa_unpack` to perform direct pointer dereferences on misaligned addresses for 16-bit and 32-bit fields, triggering unaligned memory access faults on architectures that enforce strict alignment.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states "dfa tables can originate from kernel or userspace and 8-byte alignment isn't always guaranteed" and the kernel log shows "Kernel unaligned access at TPC[8db2a8] aa_dfa_unpack+0x6e8/0x720". The patch replaces direct cast-and-dereference patterns (e.g., `*(__be16 *)blob`) with `get_unaligned_be16()` and `get_unaligned_be32()` to safely handle misaligned data.

intent_record.intent_summary: Added missing include for <linux/unaligned.h> to resolve implicit function declaration errors when using unaligned access macros.
intent_record.what: Added #include <linux/unaligned.h> between includes of <linux/kref.h> and local headers.
intent_record.how: This adds the kernel header for unaligned memory access macros, making functions like get_unaligned and put_unaligned available to the source file.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix unaligned memory access in unpack_table by using get_unaligned_be16/32 instead of direct pointer casts.
intent_record.what: Replaced direct pointer dereference casts (*(__be16 *)(blob), etc.) with get_unaligned_be16() and get_unaligned_be32() calls for reading 16-bit and 32-bit big-endian values from potentially unaligned blob buffer.
intent_record.how: Prevents unaligned memory access faults on architectures that require alignment (e.g., ARM) by using safe unaligned access helpers instead of assuming proper alignment.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential unaligned memory access by using unaligned access helpers when unpacking DFA header.
intent_record.what: Replaced direct dereferences of __be32 and __be16 pointers with get_unaligned_be32 and get_unaligned_be16 when reading header fields from a data blob.
intent_record.how: Ensures that reading of the magic number, header size, and flags from the data blob is safe even when the blob is not aligned to the natural alignment of 2 or 4 byte integers, preventing alignment faults on strict-alignment architectures.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update comment in aa_dfa_unpack to use get_unaligned_be32 instead of an unaligned pointer dereference in a commented-out code example.
intent_record.what: In a comment block within aa_dfa_unpack, a line of commented-out code is changed from using an unaligned pointer dereference to get_unaligned_be32.
intent_record.how: This change has no runtime effect; it only updates a comment to show a better practice for reading unaligned big-endian data.

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
apparmor: fix restricted endian type warnings for dfa unpack

Signed-off-by: John Johansen <john.johansen@canonical.com>
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit e6e8bf418850d7958311a96ccfb594f2bcc8313e
Author: John Johansen <john.johansen@canonical.com>
Date:   Mon Jan 16 00:43:13 2017 -0800

    apparmor: fix restricted endian type warnings for dfa unpack
    
    Signed-off-by: John Johansen <john.johansen@canonical.com>

diff --git a/security/apparmor/match.c b/security/apparmor/match.c
index 8f0806b35a75..eb0efef746f5 100644
--- a/security/apparmor/match.c
+++ b/security/apparmor/match.c
@@ -73,11 +73,11 @@ static struct table_header *unpack_
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit only changes pointer types from (u16 *) to (__be16 *) and (u32 *) to (__be32 *) for endianness correctness, but still performs direct pointer dereferences (e.g., `*(__be16 *)(blob)`, `*(__be32 *)(blob + 8)`, `*(__be32 *)data`, `*(__be16 *)(data + 12)`) on the blob. If the blob is not 8-byte aligned, these dereferences cause unaligned memory access faults on strict-alignment architectures. The root cause requires alignment-safe access (e.g., get_unaligned_be16/32), which is not introduced here. Thus, the vulnerable construct remains and the fix is absent.
